mainTopic: Which קרבנות could be brought on a private במה in the time of גלגל: the views of רבי מאיר and the רבנן, שמואל's statement about a נזיר, and the source of the חכמים
overview: This amud opens with the last words of a ברייתא listing what was brought on the big public מזבח at גלגל. The גמרא explains רבי מאיר, who learns from a פסוק that only voluntary ('fitting') offerings could go on a private במה. He counts מנחות and קרבנות of a נזיר as voluntary. The רבנן disagree: a מנחה is never brought on a private במה, and a נזיר's offerings count as חובות. שמואל first limits their argument to the נזיר's חטאת and אשם. רבה challenges this from a ברייתא that leaves out the נזיר's cooked foreleg. The גמרא then reverses שמואל's statement: the argument is about the נזיר's עולה and שלמים, and all agree his חטאת and אשם are never brought on a private במה. Finally, the גמרא gives the source of the חכמים: ״איש הישר בעיניו״ limits an individual to voluntary offerings, while the צבור may bring even obligatory ones.

steps.title: End of the list: fixed-time public obligations
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes its list of what was brought on the great public מזבח at גלגל: public חובות that have a fixed time.
steps.simpleTranslation: And obligatory offerings that have a fixed time.
steps.whatsHappening: These are the closing words of a ברייתא that started earlier. It is adding one more item to the list of what was brought on the big public מזבח: public obligations with a set time, like the תמיד and the מוסף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point of 'fixed time' is to narrow the list. Public obligations that have a set schedule went on the big public מזבח at גלגל, and public obligations without a set time did not. This finishes the ברייתא, so the גמרא can now explain the opinions inside it.

keyTerms.meaning: Obligatory offerings, ones a person or the community is required to bring
They have a fixed, scheduled time
The first place the משכן stood in ארץ ישראל, a time when private במות were allowed

phrases.english: and obligatory offerings that have a fixed time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא begun before this section
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Public obligatory offerings with a fixed time were brought on the great public מזבח at גלגל.

steps.title: Asking for רבי מאיר's source
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the reason is behind רבי מאיר's view that only voluntary offerings went on a private במה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רבי מאיר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי מאיר holds his opinion from the ברייתא. This question sets up the next step, where the גמרא brings a פסוק as his source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, רבי מאיר said that only נדרים and נדבות, which includes מנחות and קרבנות of a נזיר, were brought on a private במה in the time of גלגל. The גמרא wants to know where in the תורה this limit comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
A private altar, which was allowed at certain times before the בית המקדש

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Meir?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from quoting the ברייתא to explaining the opinions in it
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for רבי מאיר's view that only voluntary offerings may be brought on a private במה in the time of גלגל.

steps.title: The פסוק: fitting offerings yes, obligations no
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר learns from 'You shall not do all that we do here this day' that in ארץ ישראל, before the permanent מקדש, only voluntary offerings could go on a private במה. מנחות and נזירות count as voluntary.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the פסוק says: 'You shall not do all that we do here this day.' משה said to ישראל: when you enter ארץ ישראל, you may bring 'fitting' (voluntary) offerings, but you may not bring obligatory ones. מנחות and the offerings of a נזיר are 'fitting' offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק. משה tells ישראל that once they enter the land, they will not be able to bring everything they bring now in the מדבר. They may bring only voluntary offerings on private במות, and מנחות and קרבנות of a נזיר fall into that voluntary group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ישרות picks up the end of the same פסוק, 'whatever is ישר in his eyes.' Offerings a person chooses to bring on his own may go on a private במה, while חובות may not. רבי מאיר counts a נזיר's offerings as voluntary because no one is forced to become a נזיר.

keyTerms.meaning: A פסוק, a verse
'Fitting' offerings, meaning ones a person brings by his own choice (נדרים and נדבות)
You enter
Flour offerings
The offerings a נזיר brings
They are

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'You shall not do all that we do' as forbidding all קרבנות. It only cuts out the obligatory ones. Voluntary offerings are still allowed on a private במה.

phrases.english: As the verse says:
"You shall not do according to all
that we do here this day" –
Moses said to the Jewish people:
When you enter the Land of Israel –
fitting offerings you may sacrifice,
phrases.notes: This picks up the end of the same פסוק: 'whatever is ישר (fitting) in his own eyes.'

phrases.english: obligatory offerings you may not sacrifice.
Meal offerings and nazirite offerings – they are fitting offerings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about רבי מאיר's source
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק in דברים 12:8 teaches that in ארץ ישראל, before the permanent מקדש, only voluntary offerings may be brought on a private במה. מנחות and נזירות count as voluntary.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets up the dividing line, voluntary versus obligatory, that decides what may go on a private במה.

steps.title: Why the רבנן leave out מנחות and נזירות
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן agree about voluntary versus obligatory, but they hold that a מנחה is never brought on a private במה and that a נזיר's offerings count as חובות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן: there is no מנחה on a private במה, and נזיר offerings are obligatory.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the רבנן disagree with רבי מאיר about the two examples he gave. It gives a separate reason for each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For מנחות, the רבנן hold a different rule entirely: a מנחה is never offered on a private במה at all. For נזירות, they say that becoming a נזיר is a choice, but once someone is a נזיר he must bring the offerings, so they count as חובות.

keyTerms.meaning: A מנחה is not offered on a private במה

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides agree that only voluntary offerings go on a private במה. They argue about two cases. רבי מאיר says מנחות and נזירות count as voluntary. The רבנן say a מנחה never goes on a במה at all, and a נזיר's offerings are obligatory.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis –
phrases.notes: The גמרא skips a few words here. Read it as: 'And what is the reason of the רבנן?'

phrases.english: there is no meal offering on a private altar;
nazirite offerings are obligatory offerings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view, explaining why the רבנן reject רבי מאיר's two examples
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A מנחה is never brought on a private במה, and a נזיר's offerings are obligatory once he has taken the vow.

steps.title: שמואל limits the dispute to the נזיר's sin and guilt offerings
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says רבי מאיר and the רבנן argue only about the נזיר's חטאת and אשם. Everyone agrees his עולה and שלמים go on a private במה.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: The argument is only about the חטאת and the אשם. But the עולות and שלמים, everyone agrees, are proper to bring, and they are brought.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל narrows the argument from the previous steps. He says it is only about some of the נזיר's offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נזיר's offerings include a חטאת, an עולה and a שלמים, and in some cases an אשם. According to שמואל, even the רבנן agree that the עולה and שלמים go on a private במה. The argument is only about the חטאת and אשם.

keyTerms.meaning: The argument or dispute
Sin offering and guilt offering
Burnt offerings and peace offerings
Literally 'straight ones.' Here it means offerings a person may properly bring by choice

phrases.english: Shmuel said: The disagreement is about the sin offering and guilt offering,
phrases.notes: He means the argument between רבי מאיר and the רבנן about a נזיר's offerings on a private במה.

phrases.english: but regarding burnt offerings and peace offerings –
all agree they are 'fitting' ones, and they are offered.
phrases.notes: 'Fitting' means they count like offerings a person chooses to bring, so they may go on a private במה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the scope of the רבי מאיר and רבנן dispute about נזירות
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute covers only the נזיר's חטאת and אשם. All agree his עולה and שלמים are brought on a private במה.

steps.title: רבה quotes a ברייתא that leaves out the נזיר's foreleg
steps.stepSummary: רבה cites a ברייתא listing priestly gifts that apply only at the great public במה. He notes that the נזיר's cooked foreleg is missing from the list.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה objected: The breast and thigh, and the gift from the loaves of the תודה, apply at the great במה but do not apply at a small במה. Yet the cooked foreleg was left out.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה brings a source to challenge שמואל. In this step he only sets up the source and points out what is missing. The actual argument comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא suggests that these שלמים were brought on a private במה, but without giving the כהן his gifts. If the נזיר's שלמים were also brought there, the ברייתא should have listed the נזיר's foreleg too. Leaving it out hints that a נזיר's שלמים never went on a private במה at all.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised an objection from a source
The breast and thigh of a שלמים, given to the כהן
The loaves set aside for the כהן from the breads of a תודה
The cooked foreleg of the נזיר's ram, given to the כהן
He left it out

phrases.english: Rabba raised an objection:
The breast and thigh, and the teruma of the thanks-offering loaves –
apply at a great altar,
and do not apply at a small altar.
whereas the cooked foreleg – he left it out;
phrases.notes: This is רבה talking, not the ברייתא. The foreleg comes from the נזיר's ram, במדבר 6:19.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to attack שמואל's statement
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's claim that all agree the נזיר's שלמים go on a private במה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא leaves out the נזיר's foreleg. That suggests a נזיר's שלמים were not brought on a private במה at all.

steps.title: No one fits the ברייתא under שמואל's version
steps.stepSummary: If the argument is about the עולה and שלמים, the ברייתא follows the רבנן. Under שמואל's version, though, no opinion fits it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works if you say they argue about the עולה and שלמים: then whose view is this? The רבנן. But if you say they argue only about the חטאת and אשם, whose view is this?
steps.whatsHappening: רבה finishes his challenge. He shows that under שמואל's version, no one could be the author of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the רבנן hold that a נזיר's שלמים never go on a private במה, the missing foreleg makes sense, and the ברייתא follows them. But under שמואל, both רבי מאיר and the רבנן allow the נזיר's שלמים on a private במה. Then the foreleg should have been listed, and the ברייתא matches no one.

keyTerms.meaning: It works out fine if
Whose opinion is this?
They disagree

phrases.aramaic: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא בְּעוֹלָה וּשְׁלָמִים פְּלִיגִי,
phrases.english: Granted, if you say they disagree about burnt offering and peace offering,
whose is this? It is the Rabbis.
phrases.notes: The רבנן would hold the נזיר's שלמים never went on a private במה, so there was no foreleg to mention.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ בְּחַטָּאת וְאָשָׁם פְּלִיגִי,
phrases.english: But if you say they disagree about sin offering and guilt offering,
whose is this?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא בְּעוֹלָה וּשְׁלָמִים פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the objection begun in the previous step
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under שמואל, both sides allow a נזיר's שלמים on a private במה, so the foreleg should appear in the ברייתא. Its absence fits no one.

steps.title: שמואל's statement is reversed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes the wording of שמואל's statement. The argument is about the עולה and שלמים, and all agree the חטאת and אשם are never brought on a private במה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if it was said, this is how it was said. שמואל said: The argument is about the עולה and שלמים. But the חטאת and אשם, everyone agrees, are obligations and are not brought.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts רבה's challenge. It says שמואל's statement must have been said the opposite way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the רבנן hold that the נזיר's שלמים are not brought on a private במה. That explains why the ברייתא leaves out the foreleg. Even רבי מאיר agrees that the חטאת and אשם are obligations, so they are never brought on a private במה.

keyTerms.meaning: If it was said, this is how it was said. Used to correct how a statement was reported
Required offerings, not voluntary ones

steps.whatToRemember: The final version of שמואל: רבי מאיר and the רבנן argue only about the נזיר's עולה and שלמים. Everyone agrees his חטאת and אשם never go on a private במה.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two versions. The first version of שמואל was rejected; only the reversed version stands.

phrases.english: Rather, if it was stated, it was stated like this –
Shmuel said: The disagreement is about burnt offering and peace offering,
but regarding sin offering and guilt offering –

phrases.aramaic: דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל חוֹבוֹת נִינְהוּ, וְלָא קָרְבִי.
phrases.english: all agree they are obligations, and they are not offered.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves רבה's objection by reversing שמואל's statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The dispute was only about the חטאת and אשם, and all allowed the עולה and שלמים on a private במה
steps.terutzMaskana: The dispute is about the עולה and שלמים. All agree the חטאת and אשם are obligations and are not brought on a private במה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברייתא that leaves out the foreleg follows the רבנן, who do not bring the נזיר's שלמים on a private במה.

steps.title: Asking for the source of the רבנן's view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the חכמים in the ברייתא, who say the צבור could bring anything it used to bring in the אהל מועד. It then asks what their source is.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא said: 'And the חכמים say: whatever the צבור brings in the אהל מועד, etc.' What is the reason of the רבנן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to quote one line from the ברייתא, the opinion of the חכמים. It asks where they get their rule from. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים split the rule in two. The צבור could bring every kind of offering, even obligatory ones. An individual could bring only voluntary ones. The גמרא wants a source that shows this difference between the צבור and an individual.

keyTerms.meaning: The community as a whole, as opposed to one individual
The Tent of Meeting, the משכן
"What is their reason?": a request for the source of an opinion

phrases.english: The Master said:
And the Rabbis say:
Whatever the public sacrifices in the Tent, etc.
phrases.notes: "The Tent" means the אהל מועד in the מדבר. The "etc." points to the rest of the ברייתא: an individual was more limited.

phrases.english: What is the reason of the Rabbis?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After fixing the wording of שמואל's statement, the גמרא returns to the ברייתא to explain the רבנן's source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which פסוק teaches that the צבור may bring obligatory offerings during the time of במות, while an individual may not.

steps.title: The פסוק: an individual brings only what he chooses to give
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן learn from ״איש הישר בעיניו יעשה״ that an individual brings only voluntary offerings. The צבור may bring even obligatory ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'Each man, whatever is right in his eyes, he shall do.' 'A man': he may bring the 'right' offerings, meaning the voluntary ones, but not obligatory ones. The צבור, however, may bring even obligatory offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק. It reads the word איש as limiting an individual to voluntary offerings only.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks about a single 'man' and about what is 'right in his eyes', meaning what he decides on his own to give. That fits voluntary offerings, not ones he owes. The פסוק talks only about an individual, so the צבור is not limited. It may bring even חובות.

keyTerms.meaning: "A man": read here as an individual, as opposed to the צבור
He may bring (an offering)

steps.whatToRemember: According to the רבנן, ״איש הישר בעיניו״ limits an individual to voluntary offerings during the time of במות. The צבור may bring even obligatory offerings.

phrases.english: The verse says:
"Each man, whatever is right in his own eyes, he shall do";
"a man": it is "right" offerings that he may bring,
phrases.notes: "Right" offerings are the ones he decides for himself to give, meaning voluntary offerings.

phrases.english: obligatory offerings he may not bring;
but the public may bring even obligatory offerings.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא: אִישׁ הַיָּשָׁר בְּעֵינָיו יַעֲשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9 by giving the פסוק behind the רבנן's view.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words ״איש״ and ״הישר בעיניו״ in דברים 12:8 limit an individual to voluntary offerings. The צבור is not included in this limit, so it may bring even obligatory offerings.
